geos.label: South Bay
geos.blurb: San Jose, Saratoga, Sunnyvale, Mountain View

meta.standfirst: Arts, music, and worthwhile oddities, ordered by remove from Mountain View.

events.title: TAEMIN
events.note: The SHINee member's solo tour, which leans harder into choreography and a darker synth-pop palette than the group ever did. An arena booking on a Monday, which tells you how deep the K-pop audience runs here.

events.title: 53rd Safeway World Championship Pumpkin Weigh-Off
events.note: Competitive horticulture at its most absurd and most sincere: growers haul one-tonne squash in on flatbeds and a crane settles each on the scale. In-person entry is for growers; everyone else watches the livestream. Half Moon Bay is in no region list in the brief, filed Peninsula by proximity.

events.title: Indigenous Peoples' Day Sunrise Gathering
events.note: The gathering descends from the 1969-71 occupation of the island, and it begins in the dark on the parade ground with drum groups and speakers. The ceremony is free; the boat is $12 and the only way on. Dress for wind you will not believe.

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden free admission hour
events.note: The oldest public Japanese garden in the United States, free for the first hour on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays. Non-residents otherwise pay $12-16; San Francisco residents are always free with ID. Go at nine on a weekday and you will share it with almost nobody.

events.title: SF Indigenous Peoples Day with Jeremy Dutcher
events.note: Jeremy Dutcher is a Wolastoqiyik composer and tenor who builds new pieces around 1907 wax-cylinder recordings of his own community's songs, singing in a language with a few hundred speakers left. Free, outdoors, and the best thing on any Monday this month.

events.title: Bistro Moustache: French Cafe Music
events.note: Accordion-and-guitar musette and gypsy jazz in a Fillmore wine bar, no cover. The repertoire is the Paris cafe songbook played straight, which is rarer here than you would think.

events.title: Cyberpunk Cinema Night
events.note: A Cowboy Bebop episode at half six and then a feature, projected in a Mission dive bar for nothing. The free, unticketed end of The Knockout's calendar, which its ticketing widget does not carry.

events.title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night
events.note: Free with an RSVP, $20-25 without one, two-drink minimum either way. A standing Monday showcase that pulls better names than a free room should, because it books the nights the clubs do not.

events.title: Motown on Mondays
events.note: All-vinyl Motown and northern soul, running weekly since 2009 and still the most reliably good Monday in the city. Free before eight, five dollars after.

events.title: Triclops!, Wife & Gumby's Junk
events.note: Triclops! bill themselves acid-noise-prog-post-hardcore and that is not a joke at their expense — Johnny Geek's band genuinely does all of it in one song. Wife is noise rock, Gumby's Junk art-punk. One of the last autumns in this room before it closes at the end of 2026.

events.title: KiNG MALA with Jayden Hammer
events.note: Areli Castro writes sharp, slightly sinister alt-pop and sings it in a voice that keeps slipping toward a snarl. The live show is louder and more guitar-forward than the records suggest.

events.title: Love Spells with Orca
events.note: Hazy guitar-pop with a 1990s shoegaze inheritance worn openly. Two routes disagree on the room: August Hall's own page and the ticketing sweep both put it here, while the Café du Nord calendar also carries it as sold out. Going with the venue's own listing.

events.title: MARO
events.note: Portuguese singer-songwriter with a Berklee jazz training she mostly hides — close-harmony layering over almost nothing, which is why the move to Bimbo's from the Castro suits her. Relocated show; original tickets are valid.

events.title: Ludovico Einaudi
events.note: Minimalist piano loops at scale, somewhere between Satie and film score, playing to a 2,700-seat hall on the strength of streaming numbers no living composer can match. Davies has been dark since 4 October; this is the room reopening. No start time published on the route that reads.

events.title: R-Evolution sculpture: final day
events.note: Marco Cochrane's 55-foot nude steel figure comes down after a long run on the plaza. The listing's own description refers to a celebration earlier in the month, so treat the de-install date as unconfirmed — worth a look if you are passing, not worth a trip.

events.title: Town Biz Comedy Night with HellaFunny
events.note: Free with RSVP in a Temescal mezcaleria, and the lineups lean local rather than touring. HellaFunny runs most of the Bay's free comedy and this is the best-run of its Monday rooms.

events.title: Makenzie
events.note: Found only in the ticketing sweep; Yoshi's own calendar does not carry this date, and no set time or billing is published. Descriptor is lower-confidence — verify before going.

events.title: Shiner with Fotocrime
events.note: Allen Epley's Kansas City band made the loudest, most mathematical post-hardcore of the late 1990s and reformed without softening it. Fotocrime is Ryan Patterson of Coliseum doing cold, drum-machine post-punk. A 150-cap room for a band that should not fit in one.

events.title: RIN with Sabrina Sterling
events.note: German rapper whose cloud-rap melodies and Auto-Tune made him the biggest thing in Bietigheim-Bissingen and then in the country. A 500-cap room for an artist who plays arenas at home.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Broadway San Jose's touring Phantom, mid-way through a twelve-day stand. The 2,677-seat barn flatters the chandelier and does the quiet scenes no favours; book the front half of the orchestra or do not bother.

events.title: Georgian National Ballet: Sukhishvili
events.note: Eighty years of Georgian folk dance built on sword work, knee-drops onto bare boards and men landing on their toes in soft boots. Not ballet in the Western sense and all the better for it. The California Theatre is a 1927 picture palace and part of the draw.

events.title: San Jose Sharks vs Boston Bruins
events.note: The Bruins in town on a Tuesday, which is the cheapest way to see a visiting Original Six side all season. Listed for completeness; the brief deprioritises arenas.

events.title: San Francisco Botanical Garden free day
events.note: Second Tuesday of the month, free to everybody rather than residents only. The cloud-forest section is the reason to come and is at its best in damp October light.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack: free concerts and food trucks
events.note: Three hours of free lunchtime music on the plaza between the library and City Hall, with trucks. The programming is uneven and the point is that it is there at all, in a plaza that badly needs the footfall.

events.title: Lunch Rhyme with Radio XII and Paola Ramirez
events.note: Poetry read aloud at lunchtime on a downtown plaza, free, no RSVP. Downtown SF has been quietly running this kind of thing all year and nobody aggregates it.

events.title: Walking Tour: Ferry Building
events.note: An hour on the building itself — the 1898 clock tower, the nave, the freeway that hid it for thirty years. Free and better than the self-guided version.

events.title: Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty!
events.note: Japanese independent comedy, one night only, part of the run of new Japanese cinema the Roxie has been threading through October.

events.title: NAZA
events.note: Playing nearly every day this week at the Roxie, which is the Roxie telling you it believes in it. Second of its seven-day run here.

events.title: Litquake: Writing The Body, sports and identity
events.note: Michael Copperman, Swetha Amit and Yi Shun Lai on writing about bodies that are being measured. Taken from a search index rather than Litquake's own schedule, so confirm the time.

events.title: BRAINROT: a punk rock film fundraiser with live music
events.note: A screening with bands attached, raising money for the film itself. The Knockout does this better than rooms four times its size, mostly by not making it precious.

events.title: Circus By The Bay: history panel and live acts
events.note: A panel on Bay Area circus history with acts performing between the talking, in the hall at Fort Mason. Community-supported tickets are free; otherwise from $15. The kind of evening that exists nowhere else and gets announced nowhere.

events.title: Militarie Gun with Softcult, Shady Nasty & DAZY
events.note: Ian Shelton writes hardcore songs with power-pop choruses and refuses to pick a side, which is why this band outgrew the basements. Four acts for twenty dollars and DAZY alone is worth that.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Mischief's disaster-comedy Peter Pan, in which a company of catastrophically bad actors attempt the play and the set fights back. Running to 28 November on two stages' worth of machinery. The Playhouse's own calendar and ticketing pages both returned server errors this run; these times come from the production's own page, which reads.

events.title: Provoker with Topographies & Dalmatia
events.note: Bay Area darkwave with a trip-hop undertow — slow, humid, more Portishead than Sisters of Mercy. Topographies are local and genuinely good at the same trick. A hometown bill in a gilded hall that suits the mood.

events.title: Comedy Allstars
events.note: The club's standing midweek showcase. Reliable, chain-booked and ranked low by the brief for exactly that reason.

events.title: Automatic with Donzii
events.note: Bass, drums and a Juno, no guitar: the LA trio's minimal cold-wave has more in common with Suicide than with anything on a guitar-band bill. Sold out.

events.title: Dani Offline: Lover's Discourse Live, with Amanda Magana
events.note: Bedroom-pop built around spoken fragments and guitar loops, staged here as a themed show rather than a set list. Amanda Magana opens with something quieter and sadder.

events.title: Isabel LaRosa
events.note: Whispered, bass-heavy dark pop made with her brother in a bedroom and then streamed a billion times. A basement room is where this actually works.

events.title: Office Killer (4K restoration)
events.note: Cindy Sherman's only feature, a 1997 office-horror comedy that was dismissed and is now the most interesting thing a major photographer has done with a camera that moves. Restored.

events.title: Wolves of Glendale with Cor64
events.note: A comedy-adjacent trio who play pop-punk country straight enough that the jokes land harder. Cor64 does synthwave, which makes for an odd pairing and a well-sequenced night.

events.title: Zolita with Earth to Emily
events.note: Zoli Adams makes narrative queer pop and films it as serialised short cinema, so the live show is staged rather than played. The songs hold up without the videos.

events.title: The House With Laughing Windows
events.note: Pupi Avati's 1976 rural giallo, the one that swaps city glamour for a damp Emilian village and is genuinely frightening because of it. Part of Gialloween VI.

events.title: Echos with Lana Del Rabies
events.note: Echos make widescreen electronic pop; Lana Del Rabies makes industrial noise under a name that tells you the whole joke. DNA's own calendar would not open for this run, so this came off its two mirrors.

events.title: Litquake: Out on the Table, writers on food
events.note: Garrett Schlichte hosts food writers reading work that is about appetite rather than restaurants. One of a dozen Litquake nights this week that could not be read in full — the festival's schedule host refuses this run's fetches.

events.title: Litquake: Passages of Babel
events.venue: San Francisco Center for the Book
events.note: Translation and book arts together — letterpress work made from translated text, with the translators present. Servane Briand and Samuel Mignot. Time unconfirmed for the same reason as the other Litquake listings.

events.title: Live Model Tuesday Sketch
events.note: Bring a pad; a model sits, nobody teaches, the bar keeps serving. Weekly, free, and the oldest thing on Madrone's calendar.

events.title: Loathe with Fleshwater & Prostitute
events.note: Liverpool's Loathe put Deftones atmospherics on top of genuine metalcore violence and made the most-copied heavy record of the decade. Fleshwater is the Vein side project that goes full 1990s alt-rock. No start time on the route that reads.

events.title: MICO with Will Linley
events.note: Filipino-Australian singer-songwriter whose soft-grunge pop has outrun its TikTok origins. A 1,400-cap ballroom on a Tuesday is a statement of confidence. No published door time.

events.title: Oh, Mary! (opening)
events.note: Cole Escola's Mary Todd Lincoln farce opens a three-week A.C.T. run, and plays the Curran rather than either of A.C.T.'s own houses. A.C.T. publishes no curtain times anywhere on its site, which is its choice and not a fetch failure; the run is 13 October to 1 November.

events.title: Mezcal & Mole Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP, Temescal, and the Tuesday lineup is usually the loosest of the week. Food and drink are extra and the mole is the reason to arrive early.

events.title: Acoustic Alchemy
events.note: Forty years of twin-guitar instrumental jazz — one nylon-string, one steel — that sits exactly where smooth jazz and English folk overlap. An unfashionable band who have never played a sloppy set.

events.title: Bumpin Uglies with Artikal Sound System
events.note: Annapolis ska-punk that grew into American reggae without losing the shouting. Artikal Sound System are the stronger band of the two and go on first.

events.title: Drive-in movie night
events.note: Six dollars an adult, two for a child, two screens, and one of the last operating drive-ins in the Bay Area. The double bills are first-run; the experience is the listing.

events.title: Jon McLaughlin
events.note: Piano-driven singer-songwriter with a Broadway sideline, which is audible in how hard he leans on a seated room. He plays Menlo Park the following night; this is the better-sounding hall.

events.title: San Jose Barracuda vs Calgary Wranglers
events.note: A half-ten morning puck drop, which means it is a school game — rinks full of children, cheap tickets, genuinely good AHL hockey. The most atmospheric sports listing of the week and the least convenient.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Midweek performance in the twelve-day stand. Tuesday and Wednesday are the nights with seats left.

events.title: Juanes with Andrea Bejar
events.note: Thirty years of writing rock songs in Spanish that are actually rock songs rather than ballads with a guitar on them, and he still plays them like a man with something to prove. A 3,000-cap room is small for him.

events.title: Open Mic at the San Jose Improv
events.note: The club's weekly open mic. Standing programming, low information value, listed because the room is otherwise dark midweek.

events.title: Roosters Comedy Showcase
events.note: Sunnyvale's comedy club running its own midweek showcase. 21+, two-item minimum.

events.title: Jon McLaughlin: The Scenarios Tour
events.note: The second of two Bay Area nights; he played the Freight on Tuesday. The Guild is four minutes from Caltrain Menlo Park, which beats driving 101 at any hour.

events.title: Free admission day
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: YBCA's galleries are free every Wednesday, which is the single best standing deal in the city's art calendar. Dread Scott's The Body Politic and Rael San Fratello's Prototypes and Provocations are both up.

events.title: Walking Tour: Welcome to San Francisco
events.note: Two hours on foot from the Ferry Building, free. Pitched at newcomers and useful to anyone who has never been told why the streets change angle at Market.

events.title: Dance Outdoors with Rhythm & Motion
events.note: ODC's Rhythm & Motion teaching an open class on the Great Lawn for nothing. No experience assumed and no one watching who is not also doing it.

events.title: Jazz on the Plaz(a): Stevie Wonder Reimagined
events.note: Two hours of free lunchtime jazz working through the Stevie Wonder book on a downtown plaza. The Innervisions material rewards a band that can actually play it; this one usually can.

events.title: Free Art Workshop: Hand Print Art
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Drop-in printmaking in the Grand Lobby, free with registration, aimed at families but nobody checks. Two hours, no materials to bring.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Mischief's disaster-comedy Peter Pan, in which a company of catastrophically bad actors attempt the play and the set fights back. Running to 28 November on two stages' worth of machinery. The Playhouse's own calendar and ticketing pages both returned server errors this run; these times come from the production's own page, which reads.

events.title: Making Faces: puppet crafting with Creativity Explored
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Creativity Explored is the Mission studio that has supported artists with developmental disabilities since 1983, and their teaching artists run this. Drop-in, three hours, in the lobby.

events.title: The Thrift Flip: resale panel and sashiko workshop
events.note: A panel on secondhand clothing followed by instruction in sashiko, the Japanese running-stitch mending technique. The workshop is the half worth staying for.

events.title: Get Stuff Done Night
events.venue: San Francisco Public Library, Main Branch
events.note: The Jobs and Career Center stays open late so people can finish the admin they have been avoiding, with librarians on hand. Unglamorous and quietly one of the most useful things the library does.

events.title: Hanging By A Wire
events.note: One-off screening. The Roxie is running three or four distinct programmes a night this week and this is the early slot.

events.title: Salvi Soul Encuentro 2026
events.note: Five days of Salvadoran food, music and oral history in the Excelsior, free, ending with Sunday's block party. Organised by and for a community that rarely gets a listings page.

events.title: The Science Scoop: women's health breakthroughs with Holly Ingraham
events.note: A UCSF physiologist on what the field has actually established recently, free and no ticket. The Science Scoop series is the rare public-science night that does not condescend.

events.title: Wonder Workshop with magician Andrew Evans
events.venue: San Francisco Public Library, Main Branch
events.note: A working magician teaching how wonder is manufactured, in the Koret Auditorium, free. Closer to a craft lecture than a show.

events.title: Arthouse 50: 49 Square Miles Surrounded by Reality — the city envisioned by Canyon Cinema
events.note: Experimental shorts about San Francisco drawn from Canyon Cinema's distribution library, which has been the keeper of Bay Area avant-garde film since 1961. Part of the Roxie's Arthouse 50 series.

events.title: Southeast Asian art masterpieces: Angkor Wat and the Buddhas
events.venue: San Francisco Public Library, Main Branch
events.note: An hour on Khmer and Thai sculpture, free, in a library rather than a museum — which means slides, no crowd, and questions answered properly.

events.title: Assimilation (Word for Word) — preview
events.note: Word for Word stage short stories without cutting a word of them, narration included, which sounds like a gimmick until you watch it work. Here: E.L. Doctorow and Tatyana Tolstaya, directed by Rotimi Agbabiaka. First of three previews before Saturday's opening.

events.title: Infinite Bits, The Five Highs & The Genie
events.note: Three local bands in a 150-cap Mission bar whose calendar is invisible to a plain fetch and reachable only through its ticketing widget. This is the kind of bill the digest exists to find.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Mischief's disaster-comedy Peter Pan, in which a company of catastrophically bad actors attempt the play and the set fights back. Running to 28 November on two stages' worth of machinery. The Playhouse's own calendar and ticketing pages both returned server errors this run; these times come from the production's own page, which reads.

events.title: Rooftop stargazing night
events.note: Thornton Hall's roof, free, open to the public, weather permitting — and in October the fog usually loses by nine. Students run the telescopes and will let you look through them properly.

events.title: Dummy with Golomb, figure eight & sachi's mirror
events.note: LA's Dummy build krautrock engines and then bury pop melodies in them — Stereolab's method at twice the volume. Four bands, none of them filler.

events.title: Mexican Institute of Sound with Spaghetti Cumbia, Edgar & Kaefan
events.note: Camilo Lara samples Mexican brass bands, cumbia 45s and his own childhood radio into dance music that is funny without being a novelty. Spaghetti Cumbia are local and play the same trick with spaghetti-western soundtracks. The best-sequenced bill of the week.

events.title: Cowboy Beauty Queen, Duty Free & Flytrap
events.note: Local garage-punk, three bands, early enough to get home. The Knockout runs two separate things tonight and this is the one with guitars.

events.title: FIGHTMASTER with ill peach
events.note: E.R. Fightmaster's band, playing guitar-pop with a sharper lyric than the TV day job suggests. ill peach make brittle electronic pop and are the reason to be there on time.

events.title: Finn Wolfhard: The Common Side Effects Tour, with Malcy
events.note: The actor's band, and the songs are better than that sentence implies — jangly, slightly sour guitar-pop. Sold out, in a 1,400-seat picture palace, which tells you who the audience is.

events.title: Juice with Porcelain
events.note: Boston six-piece with a violin in the front line and a horn-section mentality without horns. A party band in the good sense.

events.title: Ee, Punxsutawney & Spa
events.note: Post-rock into post-rock-emo into emo-punk, which is a descending staircase the club has sequenced deliberately. Seventeen dollars for three bands in the room's last good autumn.

events.title: Filipinana
events.note: Presented by FiliKula. Rafael Manuel's film about a golf-course ball girl, shot in long static takes that turn class into geometry.

events.title: NAZA
events.note: Third day of a seven-day run. Late show tonight.

events.title: Sex Pistols with Frank Carter, plus Starcrawler and The Molotovs
events.note: Jones, Cook and Matlock with Frank Carter singing — no Lydon, and that is the whole argument. Carter is a better frontman than the band has had since 1978 and treats the songs as songs rather than relics. Starcrawler open and will outplay most of the room.

events.title: Downtown 81 Mutant Disco Dance Party
events.note: No wave, ESG, Liquid Liquid and the rest of the early-80s New York downtown canon, played on a Wednesday to people who know every record. Starts as the band night finishes.

events.title: Art Battle San Francisco City Championships
events.note: Painters get twenty minutes and an audience vote, live, in a nightclub. Competitive painting is exactly the sort of thing the brief means by worthwhile oddity. No door time published.

events.title: Halloween Costume Swap & Craft Night
events.note: Bring a costume, take a costume, make the difference up with glue. In the Loft, same building as the painting contest. No time published.

events.title: ITALO FRISCO with Nino Msk
events.note: Italo disco and cosmic synth records played properly, which in practice means a lot of 1983 twelve-inches nobody else owns. No cover published.

events.title: Litquake: Jon Ronson on men in an unravelling world
events.note: Ronson is the best living reporter on how people talk themselves into things, and the subject suits him. Time not published on any route this run could read; a two-for-one ticket deal was advertised.

events.title: Litquake: Trading Pages
events.note: Poets and fiction writers swap forms and read the result — Kate Folk, Vanessa Hua, Judy Halebsky, Dean Rader, Zach Williams. In a Mission bar, which is where Litquake is at its best. Time unconfirmed.

events.title: Patch Bay: Yoon Chung Han and Tori Sommerhof artist talks
events.note: Two artists on the technical guts of their own work, in the room where Han's Dreaming Babies: illi is installed until the 19th. Gray Area is the only route in this project's source list to experimental audiovisual work.

events.title: Tuning: live virtual session with Iana Chugunova
events.note: A working session rather than a performance — the artist builds something in front of you and explains why it is not working yet. No time published.

events.title: Exhibition tour: Maren Hassinger, Living Moving Growing
events.note: A lunchtime walk through the Hassinger survey — fifty years of wire rope, branches and plastic bags made to behave like bodies. Included with admission.

events.title: Remembering Harun Farocki
events.note: Farocki spent forty years filming how images are used to control people, which is now the only subject anyone talks about. BAMPFA's film programme is the most serious in the region and this is why.

events.title: Brit Floyd: The Moon, The Wall and Beyond
events.note: A Pink Floyd tribute with the full circular screen and quadraphonic rig, which is more than most tributes attempt. Part of the free-and-tribute circuit the brief includes but never features.

events.title: Dos Santos
events.note: Chicago five-piece who play cumbia and Andean folk forms through a psych-rock amp chain and never tip into pastiche. Twenty-nine dollars is the week's best value in a seated room.

events.title: Rip Room with Quattracenta and Fog Lamp
events.note: Rip Room are a San Francisco trio playing angular post-punk with the Wire songbook open on the floor. Thee Stork Club's own calendar reads in full now, which it did not a month ago.

events.title: Alborosie
events.note: A Sicilian who moved to Kingston at twenty-four, learned to engineer, and has made roots records good enough that the Jamaican establishment stopped asking where he was from. Rare US dates; a 300-cap club is absurd for him.

events.title: Bonnie Raitt with Jon Cleary & the Absolute Monster Gentlemen
events.note: Slide guitar played with more restraint than anyone else alive, in a 2,000-seat municipal hall rather than a shed, with Jon Cleary's New Orleans piano band opening. The one outer-region booking this week that would headline anywhere. No published curtain time.

events.title: Dracula: The Musical
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: TheatreWorks Silicon Valley's season opener, in the town the brief measures everything else from. A musical Dracula is a risk; TheatreWorks has a long record of making unlikely books work.

events.title: Rush
events.note: Lee and Lifeson touring again with a new drummer, which is the only configuration that was ever going to happen after 2020, and two nights here says the demand held. An arena show by the brief's lights; a civic event by any other measure.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Thursday of the twelve-day stand, and the last performance before the weekend's four.

events.title: Jim Perry: The Cop Comic
events.note: First of a four-night run at the Sunnyvale club. 21+, two-item minimum.

events.title: Randy Feltface: Gimmick!
events.note: A purple felt puppet doing an hour of genuinely bleak stand-up, which should not work and is the most reliable comedy ticket touring. Wait list only.

events.title: Beats, Brews & Vines
events.note: Third Thursday on Broadway at Hillcrest: a band, a beer garden and a street closed for two hours, free. The last of the season runs into October and this is the Peninsula's only free outdoor music this week.

events.title: United Nations Association Film Festival (opening)
events.note: UNAFF's 29th year of human-rights documentary, running 15-25 October across Palo Alto, Stanford and East Palo Alto. Free for students with ID. The festival's own 2026 site returned nothing readable this run, so the per-film programme and times are unconfirmed — one umbrella listing rather than a guess.

events.title: Litquake: Filipino American International Book Festival
events.venue: San Francisco Public Library, Main Branch
events.note: FilBookFest opens its Litquake-week run in the Koret Auditorium, free — readings, publishers' tables and panels. It continues through the weekend.

events.title: Chess on the Plaza
events.note: Boards set out downtown at lunchtime, free, all comers. The Mechanics' Institute has run the city's oldest chess club since 1854 and this is its pavement edition.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack: free concerts and food trucks
events.note: The second of the week's two free lunchtime sessions on the plaza. Trucks, no cover, no ticket.

events.title: Litquake: Read the Room, Books Not Bans
events.note: Banned-book readings in the alley between City Lights and Vesuvio, free, standing up. Becka Robbins, Sean Owens and Shoshana von Blanckensee among the readers.

events.title: Richard Howell's John Coltrane tribute
events.note: An Oakland tenor player who has been working the Coltrane repertoire for forty years, outdoors at lunchtime for nothing. Free Coltrane played by somebody who understands the harmony is not a small thing.

events.title: Haunted Halloween Hoopla artisan night market
events.note: Makers' market with a Halloween frame, free to browse, five hours. The artisan markets are the part of the craft-fair circuit that never reaches a ticketing platform.

events.title: The Crossing at East Cut: 5th anniversary with DJs and court opening
events.note: A ribbon-cutting on a new basketball court with DJs attached, free, on one of the few genuinely good new public spaces downtown. RSVP requested, not required.

events.title: Big Art Loop: Waterfront Walkabout art stroll
events.note: Three hours walking the public art between Pier 14 and the Exploratorium, free, with an RSVP for the guided version. The waterfront's sculpture is mostly unlabelled and this is the fix.

events.title: Third Thursdays on Treat: Trick or Treat to the Beat
events.note: A Mission side street closed off monthly with music and food, this month in costume. Free; the RSVP only gets you a dollar off a drink.

events.title: Green Film Festival (opening night)
events.note: Environmental documentary and fiction, 15-22 October, in the Richmond's repertory house. Five dollars with EBT or SNAP, which more festivals should copy. The theatre's own programme pages sit past where a plain fetch reaches.

events.title: Making History Fun Again (Clift speaker series)
events.note: A hotel running a free public history talk in its lobby bar, which is an odd place for it and exactly the sort of thing that goes unlisted. Free.

events.title: NightLife
events.note: The aquarium, the rainforest dome and the planetarium after dark with a bar in the middle, 21+. This week's framing is explicitly anti-phone — wander and talk to people. Last entry nine.

events.title: Terror Vault: 1874 Halloween haunt
events.note: Into the Dark's immersive haunt in the Old Mint's actual vaults — a building that survived 1906 with the federal gold reserve inside it, which does most of the atmospheric work. Runs many nights through Halloween; a Funcheap code takes ten dollars off.

events.title: HUMP! Film Festival (early show)
events.note: Dan Savage's touring programme of amateur short erotica, which is funnier, kinder and more varied than the premise suggests. Two shows tonight; phones are collected at the door.

events.title: Chronovisor
events.note: Second of two dates this week. Shares the building with HUMP! tonight, which makes for a strange lobby.

events.title: Assimilation (Word for Word) — preview
events.note: Second preview. Doctorow and Tolstaya staged verbatim; Z Space publishes no calendar, so this run was found by following links off its homepage.

events.title: House of Dawn, Used To Be Valentines & Courtney Jean
events.note: Three local bands, early doors, Mission bar. Reachable only through Kilowatt's ticketing widget — its own page carries no dates at all.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Mischief's disaster-comedy Peter Pan, in which a company of catastrophically bad actors attempt the play and the set fights back. Running to 28 November on two stages' worth of machinery. The Playhouse's own calendar and ticketing pages both returned server errors this run; these times come from the production's own page, which reads.

events.title: HellaFunny Thursday Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP downtown, $20-25 without. The Thursday room is the strongest of The Function's week.

events.title: Manon (San Francisco Opera)
events.note: Massenet's Manon opening a seven-performance run, and the first thing San Francisco Opera has put in the house since the company's autumn began. Thirty dollars gets you in the building; the orchestra is the reason to go.

events.title: Smuin Contemporary Ballet: French Kiss
events.note: Smuin's autumn programme, in the Fort Mason hall that no public calendar covers — this run is reachable only through the company's own production page. Three San Francisco performances left after tonight.

events.title: Edgehill with Appleseed
events.note: Melodic rock with an arena-sized chorus in a 300-cap room. Thirty dollars is steep for the size; the band are betting you will say you saw them here.

events.title: Hot Flash Heat Wave with Carpool Tunnel & Starzdust
events.note: A San Francisco band who left for LA and come back to rooms this size out of affection rather than necessity. Carpool Tunnel are also local and better live than on record.

events.title: Imperial Teen, Kids on a Crime Spree, Crows of Poundsign & Track Star
events.note: Roddy Bottum's band, thirty years of the sweetest-sounding songs anyone from Faith No More was ever going to write, on a bill of three other Bay Area bands who all still exist. Twenty dollars and a near-complete map of a local scene.

events.title: Kelsey Lu
events.note: Classically trained cellist who loops herself into something closer to ambient gospel, and whose live shows have a staged, almost liturgical shape. The gilded hall is the right room for it.

events.title: Syd Taylor with Theo Moss
events.note: Quiet, close-miked songwriting in a basement that was built for it. No cover published.

events.title: World Famous Pets with Andrew St. James
events.note: Local guitar band in a room with a fish tank behind the bar. Andrew St. James has been the most promising songwriter in the city for about a decade now and is overdue.

events.title: Abracadabra with Galore & Rhymies
events.note: Eighteen dollars for three bands who all sound like they recorded in the same damp basement in 1991, which is a compliment. Doors at eight, music at quarter to nine.

events.title: 16th & Mission Open Mic
events.note: No microphone, no stage, no permission: people take turns on the plaza and the crowd keeps quiet for whoever is up. Running for years, free, and the most purely San Francisco listing in this digest.

events.title: After Dark Industrial Dance Party
events.note: EBM, coldwave and the harder end of 1980s industrial, in a bar small enough that the room is the sound system. Monthly-ish and consistently full.

events.title: HUMP! Film Festival (late show)
events.note: Second screening of the same programme. The late house is the rowdier one.

events.title: Inner Circle dance party
events.note: Free with RSVP, weekly, and the DJs are better than a no-cover Thursday has any right to. 21+.

events.title: Level Up Thursdays: video DJ dance party
events.note: Music videos mixed live on the screens as well as the records, free, until two. Standing weekly night on Folsom.

events.title: Gautier Capucon, Lisa Batiashvili & Jean-Yves Thibaudet
events.note: Cello, violin and piano, three soloists who each headline on their own, playing chamber music together — which is the format where you hear whether they actually listen to each other. These three do. No start time on the route that reads.

events.title: Lila Downs
events.note: Three nights in the main hall from a singer who has spent thirty years setting Mixtec and Zapotec song against big-band jazz arrangements, and who sings politics without ever sounding like a pamphlet. The most substantial residency in the city this week. SFJAZZ publishes no start times on the only route that reads.

events.title: Oppidan
events.note: Melodic house in a 1,000-cap SoMa club. 1015's own site renders its calendar client-side and fetches empty, so this came off the ticketing sweep with no time or price.

events.title: Rawayana
events.note: Venezuelan band making exile pop — reggae-inflected, breezy on the surface, and pointed underneath, which is what won them a Grammy and got them denounced at home. No published door time; Songkick's venue calendar is the route.

events.title: The Blasting Company
events.note: The band who wrote the music for Over the Garden Wall, playing it live — vaudeville, Appalachian ballad and brass-band forms assembled into something genuinely strange. An audience that knows every word of a cartoon soundtrack. No door time published.

events.title: Young Miko
events.note: Puerto Rican rapper who went from tattoo artist to arena headliner in about four years and did it without softening the delivery. Arena, so the brief lists it and does not feature it. No published time on any route that reads.

events.title: Autumn Lights Festival (night one)
events.note: Seven acres of the Lake Merritt gardens filled with illuminated sculpture and projection for three nights, with the installations made by Bay Area artists rather than bought in. Free for under-fives, $12.51 for children. Go the first night; Saturday is the crush.

events.title: Collaborations with Cairo's Cimatheque
events.note: Work from and with Cimatheque, the independent film space in downtown Cairo that has been the only alternative exhibition venue in Egypt for a decade. Nothing else in the region programmes this.

events.title: Disney On Ice: Find Your Hero
events.note: Four days in the arena. Listed for completeness; the brief deprioritises arenas and this one needs no help being found.

events.title: POC Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP in Temescal. The strongest-booked of the four free HellaFunny nights in this week's digest.

events.title: Boy Harsher with james K, True Blue & Kassie Krut
events.note: Minimal synth and a voice that stays almost affectless over it, staged with the house lights off and a lot of strobe. A deep bill: Kassie Krut and True Blue are both worth arriving for. Take BART; downtown Oakland garages shut their gates at seven.

events.title: Christine Tassan et les Imposteures
events.note: A Montreal all-women quartet playing Django Reinhardt's repertoire and then pushing it into Quebecois song, which the manouche purists dislike and which is the point. No published time on the mirror that reads.

events.title: Copeathetic with Beat Cuntz and 6IXLEGS
events.note: Local hardcore, three bands. The mirror that carries this bill runs the support names together, so the billing may be two acts or three. No door time published.

events.title: Musiq Soulchild
events.note: Philadelphia neo-soul in a 400-seat jazz club, which is a tenth of the size he could sell. Two nights. The venue lists the run as a date range rather than per-show times, so check your ticket.

events.title: San Jose Barracuda vs Calgary Wranglers
events.note: The evening half of the Calgary pair, and a far more civilised hour than Wednesday's. Minor-league hockey, cheap, walkable from downtown.

events.title: Are You Garbage? Army of Garbage Tour
events.note: Class-anxiety comedy as a podcast live show, which plays much better in a room than in headphones.

events.title: Blade Rave: a vampire-themed rave
events.note: The Blade blood-rave scene restaged as an actual club night, which is both the stupidest and the most committed idea on this week's calendar. Dress accordingly.

events.title: Dracula: The Musical
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: TheatreWorks, second performance of the week. Downtown Mountain View, three minutes from Caltrain.

events.title: Maher Zain
events.note: Swedish-Lebanese singer whose devotional pop is enormous across the Muslim world and almost unlisted in American media, which is precisely the gap this digest is for. A 3,000-seat room that will be full.

events.title: St. Paul & The Minneapolis Funk All Stars
events.venue: Carriage House Theatre, Montalvo Arts Center
events.note: Paul Peterson played in The Time and in Prince's orbit for forty years, and this band is the Minneapolis rhythm section doing that repertoire without a tribute's reverence. A 300-seat carriage house on a Villa Montalvo hillside is an absurdly good room for funk.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Friday night of the run, and the first of four performances in three days.

events.title: The Wallflowers
events.note: Jakob Dylan's band on a hillside above Saratoga, playing to the vineyard terrace. They play the Fillmore on Sunday; this is the version with a view and a twenty-dollar shuttle up the hill.

events.title: Jim Perry: The Cop Comic
events.note: Second of four nights in Sunnyvale.

events.title: San Jose Bike Party (October ride)
events.note: Third Friday, meet half seven, roll at eight: several thousand people on bicycles with sound systems, through streets that are otherwise given over to cars. The start point is announced the week of the ride and the route is the event.

events.title: Small Town Murder (live podcast)
events.note: True crime done as a two-man comedy act, touring to a 1,100-seat 1927 picture palace. The venue is better than the format deserves.

events.title: Mike Salazar (en espanol)
events.note: Late Spanish-language set at the Improv. The club runs these regularly and they are almost never listed in English-language roundups.

events.title: Johnny Chay
events.note: Late Friday at the Sunnyvale club, 21+, six minutes' walk from Caltrain Sunnyvale and street parking free after six.

events.title: Dom Dolla
events.note: Melbourne tech-house in a 1941 livestock arena, which is a funnier booking than the promoters intend. Ninety-nine dollars. Daly City is in no region list in the brief; filed Peninsula by proximity to Colma.

events.title: Shovels & Rope with Nolan Taylor
events.note: Michael Trent and Cary Ann Hearst swap instruments mid-song and play louder than a duo should be able to. The Guild's ticket link carries a 17 October date while the listing says the 16th — check before travelling.

events.title: Jenny Kerr Band with The Keller Sisters
events.note: Bay Area roots-rock in the small room behind the Fox, and one of very few live-music listings on the Peninsula this week. No published door time.

events.title: Nightfall at Filoli
events.note: The Woodside estate's gardens lit and scored after dark, nightly from 26 September to 1 November. Filoli's calendar is mostly tours and tastings; this and Autumn Days are the two things on it that are listings. No per-night times published.

events.title: Politics is a Funny Business: art and poster exhibit opening
events.note: Campaign posters and political cartooning hung in a waterfront cafe's back room, free opening. The kind of show that exists for two weeks and is never written up.

events.title: Mirus Gallery presents: Nostalgia
events.note: Group show opening, free. Mirus has been the most consistent of the city's figurative-contemporary galleries for a decade.

events.title: Union Square Dances
events.note: Three hours of open-air social dancing in the square, free, with instruction at the start for whoever turns up not knowing the steps.

events.title: Free outdoor movie night
events.note: Parkside and Sunset's own free screening, with food and popcorn included. The least-publicised of the three free outdoor films tonight and the most neighbourhood-scaled.

events.title: Movies at Mechanics' Presents
events.note: Friday-evening film in the 1854 library's own screening room at 57 Post Street. The route that carries the date gives no title and no price — the institute's own page sits past where a plain fetch reaches.

events.title: Salvi Soul Encuentro 2026
events.note: Third evening of the five-day Salvadoran culture gathering in the Excelsior. Free.

events.title: Sundown Cinema outdoor movie night
events.note: A free film projected in the Dogpatch waterfront park. Bring a blanket and more layers than the forecast suggests; the wind comes off the bay all evening.

events.title: The Scout
events.note: First of three screenings this weekend. The Roxie is running seven distinct programmes tonight across its two screens and the New People Cinema in Japantown.

events.title: Jigoku (4K restoration)
events.note: Nobuo Nakagawa's 1960 Buddhist-hell film, the one that goes from a drunk-driving melodrama into forty minutes of genuinely upsetting damnation imagery. Restored, and programmed by the Roxie into the Japantown screen.

events.title: Mission Rock Fall Friday Night Movies: Ratatouille
events.note: Free, on the grass by the water at Mission Rock, with the ballpark across the channel. The right film for a park full of children and the correct choice of Pixar.

events.title: Floating Features: The Game
events.note: Fincher's San Francisco paranoia film, shown in San Francisco, as part of the Roxie's Floating Features strand. The city is the second lead.

events.title: Golden Gate Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP, 21+, downtown. The Function runs two separate free shows tonight; this is the longer one.

events.title: HellaSecret: Crazy Funny Asians comedy showcase
events.note: Two sets, free with RSVP and a suggested $5-10 donation, $15-20 otherwise. The address goes out the day before — which is the format, not an obstacle.

events.title: NAZA
events.note: Fifth day of a seven-day run.

events.title: Printz Dance Project: Six Degrees of PDP
events.note: Printz has been making jazz-inflected contemporary dance in the Mission for twenty years and this is a company retrospective rather than a new piece. ODC's calendar is the only route to this house and was absent from this project's sources until last week.

events.title: Smuin Contemporary Ballet: French Kiss (ASL interpreted)
events.note: The ASL-interpreted performance of Smuin's autumn programme at Fort Mason. Two San Francisco dates left after this.

events.title: Sweet Plot and Tom Relling Band
events.note: Two local bands, early, before the bar turns into a disco at ten. Kilowatt runs both tonight.

events.title: Assimilation (Word for Word) — preview
events.note: Final preview before Saturday's opening. Doctorow and Tolstaya staged word for word, narration included.

events.title: Neurosis with Kowloon Walled City
events.note: Neurosis invented the thing everyone now calls post-metal, in Oakland, and then stopped playing almost entirely. Two nights at the Fillmore is the most consequential heavy booking the Bay has had in years, and Kowloon Walled City are the right local band to open it.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Mischief's disaster-comedy Peter Pan, in which a company of catastrophically bad actors attempt the play and the set fights back. Running to 28 November on two stages' worth of machinery. The Playhouse's own calendar and ticketing pages both returned server errors this run; these times come from the production's own page, which reads.

events.title: Renny Conti with James Eichman
events.note: Soft-focus guitar-pop in the basement while Allan Rayman plays the hall upstairs in the same building. Two rooms, one door, one calendar.

events.title: Sara Bareilles with Celisse
events.note: Two nights in the Civic's theatre configuration. Celisse is the far more interesting guitarist of the two and opens both. BART or Muni to Civic Center; the garage is $45.

events.title: Tainted Love
events.note: The Bay Area's long-running 1980s cover band, and a fixture of the free-concert and ballroom circuit. Included for completeness; never the best thing on a Friday.

events.title: The Confessional (improv)
events.note: Audience confessions turned into scenes on the spot, in the Mission. Twelve dollars with the Funcheap code. Endgames runs three shows back to back tonight.

events.title: The Jungle Giants with Morning Silk
events.note: Brisbane band who swapped guitars for sequencers somewhere around 2019 and got much bigger for it. Twenty dollars at the low end is the cheapest ticket in the hall this week.

events.title: The Stoner Comedy Jam
events.note: Free with RSVP in a cannabis lounge off Market, 21+ with ID and a one-item minimum. Exactly as advertised.

events.title: The History of Concrete
events.note: A documentary on the material that built the twentieth century and is now its largest carbon problem. Plays again Saturday.

events.title: Allan Rayman
events.note: Rayman works through invented characters and refuses interviews, which would be tiresome if the songs were not good. 21+. This show is missing from the hall's usual mirror and appears only on the building's own calendar.

events.title: Hausu
events.note: Nobuhiko Obayashi's 1977 haunted-house film, in which a cat eats a piano and nothing is explained. Programmed on the Japantown screen beside Jigoku, which is the correct double bill.

events.title: Jessie Ware with Dhruv
events.note: Ware spent a decade as a torch singer and then made the best straight-ahead disco records of the 2020s, and the live show commits fully to the second version. A second night was added for Saturday, which answers the question.

events.title: Psyched! Fest with Diles Que No Me Maten
events.note: A one-room psych and punk mini-festival headlined by a Spanish-language hardcore band named after a Rulfo story. Five acts for twenty-five dollars.

events.title: The Seshen with Sweet Lew & Cardboard People
events.note: A long-running Bay Area group whose electronic soul has aged better than almost anything from the same moment, on a bill with Sweet Lew's Chicano southwest soul. Seventeen dollars for three local bands, which is the room's whole case for existing.

events.title: Amélie Farren, Lilith Max & Rabbitology: The Three Wishes Tour
events.note: A co-headline of three songwriters touring as a package rather than a hierarchy, which makes for a longer and better-paced night than the usual support slot. They play Felton the following evening.

events.title: Love T.K.O. Disco Dance Party
events.note: Seventies soul and disco on vinyl. The venue's ticketing widget carries this night twice under two links; it is one party.

events.title: Olive Klug with Frail Talk
events.note: Queer folk songwriting with a comic timing that defuses the earnestness before it sets. The crowd sings along to every word, which is either the appeal or the warning.

events.title: SF Neo-Futurists: The Infinite Wrench
events.note: Thirty plays in sixty minutes, order decided by the audience shouting numbers, price set by a die roll at the door. Weekly, and the single best value in San Francisco theatre.

events.title: This Is Lorelei with Colin Miller
events.note: Nate Amos writing songs that sound like a 1970s AM radio dial being turned, and singing them completely straight. Sold out. Colin Miller is from the same North Carolina circle and worth the early door.

events.title: Yamagucci, Izik & Amiss
events.note: Doors at nine in a 500-cap SoMa room. No price published.

events.title: Your Fucked Up Relationship (improv)
events.note: Same company, later slot, the premise in the title. The late houses at Endgames are looser and funnier than the early ones.

events.title: 3rd Annual Graveyard Shift
events.note: An all-night horror marathon closing the Roxie's Arthouse 50 celebration. Half nine start and no stated end, which is the point.

events.title: Putos Discos with DJ Nino
events.note: Latin dance records in a Mission bar until late, following the band bill. Ten o'clock start.

events.title: GorillaT
events.note: Bass music and Memphis-leaning rap edits. One of only two DNA listings this week, because the club's own calendar refuses the fetch this digest is compiled with — see Thin this week.

events.title: Lester T. Raww: FALLING OUT, music from Fallout
events.note: The Fallout soundtrack's 1940s swing and crooner material played live by a band in costume, which is a more coherent idea than it sounds. Madrone runs a second night, Wild Card, alongside it.

events.title: Lila Downs
events.note: Second of three nights. No start times are published on the only SFJAZZ route that reads.

events.title: Oshe
events.note: The Great Northern's JamBase page reports the venue as having nothing on at all this week, so this came off the ticketing sweep with no time or price.

events.title: Public Works 16th anniversary: Detroit Love with Carl Craig and Octave One
events.note: Carl Craig is the most important living Detroit techno producer and Octave One play theirs live on hardware rather than DJing it. A 16th-birthday booking a club twice this size would struggle to land. No door time published; the venue's calendar gives none.

events.title: Yasmina
events.note: House and techno in the main room. From the ticketing sweep; 1015's own calendar does not read.

events.title: You're Welcome in the Loft
events.note: Rachel Torro, Benjamin K and Little Lord in the upstairs room while Detroit Love runs the main floor. Taken from the venue's social post rather than its calendar, so treat the billing as provisional.

events.title: moe.
events.note: Thirty-five years of jam-band improvisation with better songwriting underneath it than the genre's reputation allows. A ballroom floor and no seats is the correct format. No door time published.

events.title: Mosse Lecture: Stefanie Schulte Strathaus on curating living archives
events.note: The former head of Arsenal in Berlin on what it means to keep a film archive in use rather than in storage. Specialist, and the specialists are the audience.

events.title: NFL Stories with Peter King and Carmen Policy
events.note: The reporter who covered the league for thirty years and the executive who built the 49ers dynasty, in conversation in a shop. Free; pay what you can to reserve a seat.

events.title: Friday Nights at OMCA with MacArthur Maze: Black Panther Party at 60
events.note: The Panthers were founded in Oakland in October 1966 and OMCA holds the archive, so the sixtieth falls to this museum to mark — galleries open, food trucks, and MacArthur Maze on the Garden Stage. Free. Only a handful of Friday Nights remain before the series stops for winter.

events.title: Pleasant Hill Night Market
events.note: Food stalls, makers and music in a suburban park, free. Pleasant Hill is in no region list in the brief; filed East Bay by proximity to Concord.

events.title: Autumn Lights Festival (night two)
events.note: Second of three nights of illuminated installations through the lakeside gardens. Friday is busier than Thursday and calmer than Saturday.

events.title: HellaSecret speakeasy comedy and cocktail night
events.note: Free with a limited code, five dollars off otherwise. Address released the day of the show.

events.title: Raging Bull
events.note: Scorsese on 35mm terms in a proper theatre, which is the only way the fight photography makes sense. BAMPFA pairs it with The King of Comedy on Sunday.

events.title: ScHoolboy Q: 10 Years of Blank Face LP
events.note: Blank Face is the best album anyone in Black Hippy made and the one Q has been least willing to play in full, so a tenth-anniversary run is a genuine occasion. A 2,800-cap art deco room suits it. Take BART.

events.title: Vulfpeck with Jackie Evans
events.note: A studio-rat funk band who became a stadium act by being audibly better musicians than anyone else on the bill, and who still mic the drums like it is 1972. An October night in a hillside amphitheatre; bring a coat.

events.title: glaive with Kurtains
events.note: One of the few hyperpop-adjacent writers from that 2020 moment whose songs have got better rather than louder. All ages, which is the UC Theatre's whole purpose.

events.title: Black Girl Magic: 10th anniversary show
events.note: A decade of a party built by and for Black women in downtown Oakland, which in a city this gentrified is a real anniversary. Until half one.

events.title: Altan
events.note: Forty years of Donegal fiddle music played at a tempo that only works if everyone in the band is listening, with Mairéad Ní Mhaonaigh singing. The Freight is a listening room and this is the week's best argument for one. No time on the mirror that reads.

events.title: Disney On Ice: Find Your Hero
events.note: Second day of the four-day arena run. Listed for completeness.

events.title: Musiq Soulchild
events.note: Second night of the Yoshi's run. The venue publishes the run as a date range, not per-show times.

events.title: Petty Theft
events.note: Tom Petty covers, done well, in a Shattuck beer hall. Part of the circuit the brief includes and never features.

events.title: Spike Hellis
events.note: LA duo making hardware-only EBM that is genuinely hostile rather than retro-stylish. A small Oakland room is the correct setting. No published time.

events.title: The Stitches with Hunting Lions, Loud Graves & SF Rejects
events.note: Los Angeles snot-punk from the late 1990s, still playing the same two and a half minutes per song. Four bands in a 150-cap Albany room. No door time published.

events.title: 31st Annual Campbell Oktoberfest
events.note: Campbell Avenue closed for the day: free to walk in, pay for what you eat and drink, with a children's area and two stages. Thirty-one years makes it the South Bay's most established street festival and it is still almost never written up outside the city's own newsletter.

events.title: Day Trip Festival NorCal, day one
events.note: Insomniac's Day Trip makes its Northern California debut on a downtown San Jose park: Gordo back-to-back with Vintage Culture, an Eli Brown sunset set, Wax Motif, J. Worra, Lefty and Script. Eight hours of open-air house and techno, 18+, and the nearest region in the brief gets the biggest music event of the week.

events.title: Dracula: The Musical (matinee)
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: TheatreWorks matinee in downtown Mountain View, three minutes from Caltrain.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera (matinee)
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Saturday matinee. The cheaper of the day's two performances and the one with seats.

events.title: R&B Fest
events.note: An afternoon R&B session at the Sunnyvale club, starting at three, which is unusual enough to note. 21+.

events.title: Ghoul with Dry Socket
events.note: Oakland's masked thrash band, who have kept the bit going for twenty years and play faster than most bands who take themselves seriously. Dry Socket are local hardcore.

events.title: Jim Perry: The Cop Comic
events.note: Third of four nights, and an earlier curtain than the weeknights.

events.title: Dracula: The Musical
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Saturday evening performance of TheatreWorks' season opener.

events.title: Rush
events.note: Second San Jose night. Arena, so listed and not featured; two sold nights in a 17,000-seat room is its own argument.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Saturday evening, the busiest performance of the twelve-day stand.

events.title: GORDO
events.note: The official Day Trip afterparty, 21+, a thirty-minute drive from Discovery Meadow and the only way to see Gordo twice in a day.

events.title: Dustin Nickerson
events.note: Three shows across Saturday and Sunday, marked almost sold out. The club does not publish per-show times for the weekend run.

events.title: Nelly
events.note: Country Grammar is twenty-six years old and Nelly still performs it like a man who knows exactly which four songs the hillside came for. A vineyard amphitheatre is a strange room for St. Louis rap and it works. No published curtain time.

events.title: Pedro Fernandez
events.note: Ranchera and mariachi from a singer who has been a star in Mexico since he was a child actor. Found in the ticketing sweep only; the venue's own mirror does not carry this date, so confirm before travelling.

events.title: 54th Annual Half Moon Bay Art & Pumpkin Festival
events.note: Main Street closed for two days of pumpkin carving, a costume parade, four stages and the aftermath of Monday's weigh-off. Free, fifty-four years old, and the one event this week that an entire region organises its weekend around. Highway 92 is the bottleneck; go early or take the shuttle. Half Moon Bay is in no region list in the brief, filed Peninsula by proximity.

events.title: San Francisco Opera costume treasure hunt and sale
events.note: The company's own scene shop opened up and the racks made available — forty years of costume stock, by appointment. The brief's hard filter lists the word sale, but its stated reason is commerce wearing a culture costume, and this is the literal inverse; an editorial call, flagged in the report.

events.title: 4th Annual Indie Author Fest and Book Fair
events.note: Self-published authors with tables, plus panels on getting a book out without a publisher. Free; the books cost money. The Peninsula's answer to Litquake and a fraction of its size.

events.title: Twilight Nature Walk at the Baylands
events.note: Ninety minutes into the Baylands as the light goes, free, led by naturalists. October is when the shorebirds come back in numbers.

events.title: Autumn Days at Filoli
events.note: The daytime half of Filoli's autumn programme, 26 September to 1 November, with the gardens planted and dressed for the season. No per-day times published on the estate's events index.

events.title: United Nations Association Film Festival
events.note: Weekend screenings in the Palo Alto run of the human-rights documentary festival. Free for students with ID. The per-film programme could not be read this week; see What could not be reached.

events.title: 38th Annual SF Old Car Picnic
events.note: Several hundred pre-1975 cars parked on the grass of the old Speedway Meadow, free to walk among. Forty dollars to bring a car, ten to bring a bicycle. The best free people-watching in the park and it finishes before the T-Pain crowd arrives.

events.title: Free museum day for Bay Area residents
events.note: Free for Bay Area residents with ID, timed tickets required and they go. The de Young's own site answers every automated fetch with a bot challenge, so this is read off a listings page rather than the museum's.

events.title: Free museum day for Bay Area residents
events.note: Same museum group, same free Saturday, and a far shorter queue than the de Young's. Timed tickets and ID required.

events.title: Filipino American International Book Festival
events.venue: San Francisco Public Library, Main Branch
events.note: Its main day in the Koret Auditorium: readings, panels and publishers' tables, free. Part of Litquake's week and the best-organised thing in it.

events.title: Secondhand Saturday with Sunset Mercantile
events.note: Vintage and resale sellers out on the Sunset's market block, free to browse. Six hours, and the inner Sunset's own calendar rather than a city-wide one.

events.title: 2026 Bay Area Science Festival
events.note: The festival's main day: several hundred hands-on exhibits run by working researchers, free, no ticket. Aimed at children and genuinely interesting to adults who ask questions.

events.title: Shipyard Open Studios, Fall 2026
events.note: Three hundred artists' studios in the shipyard buildings, open, free, with free parking — the largest artist colony on the West Coast and twice a year the only way in. The city-wide ArtSpan schedule was again unconfirmable this year; this one is certain.

events.title: ZYZZYVA Movie Matinee: Amarcord (35mm)
events.note: Fellini's memory film on 35mm at lunchtime, introduced by Ingrid Rojas Contreras for ZYZZYVA. A print, a writer and a matinee — about as good as repertory gets.

events.title: NAZA
events.note: The Japantown screening of the week's most-played title.

events.title: T-Pain with Ari Lennox (R&B and Ribs)
events.venue: Robin Williams Meadow, Golden Gate Park
events.note: The R&B and Ribs party moves into Golden Gate Park for the first time, with T-Pain headlining and Ari Lennox before him, all ages, barbecue throughout. An afternoon show, which makes it the rare park concert you can do and still have an evening.

events.title: Joe Bataan (Yerba Buena Gardens Festival)
events.note: Bataan invented Latin soul in Spanish Harlem in 1967 by putting doo-wop singing over a boogaloo band, and at eighty-four he still fronts it himself. Two and a half hours, outdoors, free, with an RSVP. Nothing else this week is both this historically important and this cheap.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Mischief's disaster-comedy Peter Pan, in which a company of catastrophically bad actors attempt the play and the set fights back. Running to 28 November on two stages' worth of machinery. The Playhouse's own calendar and ticketing pages both returned server errors this run; these times come from the production's own page, which reads.

events.title: Smuin Contemporary Ballet: French Kiss (audio described)
events.note: The audio-described matinee of Smuin's autumn programme. Penultimate San Francisco performance.

events.title: The Ceremony (film series)
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Fifteen dollars including themed snacks and gallery admission, in YBCA's screening room. The galleries alone are worth the ticket.

events.title: Walking Tour: bar and cocktail history
events.note: An hour and three quarters on the financial district's drinking history, free, on foot. The Pisco Punch story alone justifies it.

events.title: First They Came for My College
events.note: A documentary on political pressure applied to universities, on the Japantown screen the Roxie programmes.

events.title: Market Street Arts & Theater Festival
events.note: Six blocks of mid-Market, three public plazas, 104 partners and more than fifty performances, nearly all free: the kickoff at UN Plaza has Dear San Francisco, BANDALOOP dancing down a building and drag laureate D'Arcy Drollinger. First year. The most ambitious free programming the street has seen in a decade and the single best use of a Saturday evening.

events.title: NAZA
events.note: Two showings today on the Roxie's own screens plus one in Japantown. Sixth day of the run.

events.title: The Annual Scott Alcoholocaust Memorial Roast and Rock n' Roll Birthday Bash-O!
events.note: A memorial roast for a Mission punk promoter, with bands, starting at four in the afternoon and running as long as it runs. Unlistable anywhere but here and the reason this venue is worth the effort of reaching.

events.title: The Match Factory Girl
events.note: Kaurismäki's seventy-minute masterpiece of almost no dialogue, which is the funniest and bleakest film in his trilogy about Finnish working life.

events.title: Jigoku (4K restoration)
events.note: Second of three weekend showings of the restored 1960 Japanese hell film.

events.title: The Scout
events.note: Second of three weekend screenings.

events.title: Crazy Funny Asians comedy showcase
events.note: Free with RSVP downtown, $25 otherwise. The touring showcase's San Francisco home room.

events.title: Date My EX!
events.note: A live dating show in which people set up their former partners, performed in a Mission bar. Early, then the disco takes over at ten.

events.title: Let Her Sing 2026: a celebration of female voices
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: A gala concert in the Blue Shield theatre. The ticket price puts it well above the rest of this digest; the bill is the argument.

events.title: Assimilation (Word for Word) — opening night
events.note: Opening night after three previews. Word for Word stage Doctorow and Tolstaya without cutting a sentence, which turns prose rhythm into blocking. Runs to 8 November.

events.title: Lewis OfMan with Lealani
events.note: French producer making bright, slightly goofy synth-pop with real chord changes under it. Bimbo's velvet and fish tank suit him better than a warehouse would.

events.title: Lost Highway
events.note: Lynch's least-explicable feature, which is saying something, and the one whose soundtrack has aged into a period document. Late Saturday is the right slot for it.

events.title: Neurosis with Kowloon Walled City (second night)
events.note: Second Fillmore night. If you can only make one, Saturday is the one with the louder room and the longer set.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Mischief's disaster-comedy Peter Pan, in which a company of catastrophically bad actors attempt the play and the set fights back. Running to 28 November on two stages' worth of machinery. The Playhouse's own calendar and ticketing pages both returned server errors this run; these times come from the production's own page, which reads.

events.title: Puff Puff Laugh
events.note: Free with RSVP in the cannabis lounge, 21+ with ID and a one-item minimum. The Saturday version of Friday's room.

events.title: Sara Bareilles with Celisse
events.note: Second of two nights in the Civic's theatre configuration. Civic Center BART is three minutes away and the garage is $45.

events.title: The Confessional (improv)
events.note: Mission improv built from audience confessions. Twelve dollars with the code and the cheapest theatre ticket in the city.

events.title: The History of Concrete
events.note: Second screening of the concrete documentary, opposite Lost Highway on the other screen.

events.title: Jessie Ware with Dhruv (second night)
events.note: The added second night, which means Friday sold out. Same disco-revue staging, same support.

events.title: heavens to betsy with Street Eaters & The Lilies
events.note: Corin Tucker and Tracy Sawyer's band, the one that came before Sleater-Kinney and made two records of riot grrrl at its least compromised, playing two nights in a 350-cap room. This has not happened in thirty years and will not again. Street Eaters are the correct Bay Area postpunk support.

events.title: Asha Banks with Alfie Jukes
events.note: British songwriter on a first headline run, in a room that is the right size for exactly one more album cycle.

events.title: Ella Boh: Blurry Tour
events.note: Doors at eight, show at nine. Thirty-six dollars is high for the room, which usually signals a short tour and a motivated audience.

events.title: Flower Face with Stella Prince
events.note: Ruby McKinnon writes very quiet songs about very bad years and an audience that found her on the internet sings them back. Twenty dollars.

events.title: HellaSecret: Desi Comedy Night
events.note: Free for the first hundred with an RSVP, $25 at the door, address released the day before. Two sets.

events.title: Love Supreme / Continental Drift dance party
events.note: The ticketing widget lists two differently named parties in this room at the same hour — Continental Drift's global grooves and Love Supreme's San Francisco edition — which the venue's own guidance says to read as one night under two billings.

events.title: SF Neo-Futurists: The Infinite Wrench
events.note: Thirty plays in sixty minutes, audience-ordered, price decided by a die. The Saturday house is the fuller one.

events.title: Tom Hamilton with Eric Silverman
events.note: The American Babies guitarist solo, which means long-form improvisation rather than songs. 21+, basement, late start.

events.title: Drunk Theatre Halloween special
events.note: A scripted show performed by a cast getting progressively less able to perform it. The Halloween edition adds costumes to the variables.

events.title: DJ Dave Paul presents: Groove Is In The Heart
events.note: Dave Paul has been running the Bay's best 1990s hip-hop and funk nights since the actual 1990s. Ten o'clock, after the dating show clears out.

events.title: 250 Years, Indigenous Futures (Haines Gallery)
events.note: A group show at Haines' Fort Mason space running to 7 November, answering the semiquincentennial with contemporary Native work. Free; the campus index gives no hours.

events.title: Akeem Ali: The Texture Tour
events.note: Soul singing with a rapper's phrasing. August Hall's listings carry no times or prices; the ticket link is the only route to either.

events.title: Arion Press public tour
events.note: Third Saturday of the month inside one of the last working letterpress and type-foundry operations in the country, at Fort Mason. Monotype casting, hand-set pages, editions still sold. No time or price on the campus events index.

events.title: BATS Improv: Trick or Treat
events.note: BATS' Halloween long-form show at Fort Mason, playing this Saturday and the next. The company's page gives no time or price, only an Eventbrite link.

events.title: Daniel Sloss
events.note: The Scottish comedian whose hour on relationships has reportedly ended thousands of them. The venue's calendar carries a cancelled duplicate of this date alongside the live one; the live row is the one listed here.

events.title: FRINGE: the indie rock dance party
events.note: Guitar records played for dancing rather than nodding. Madrone also has Jim Washington in the other slot tonight. No cover published.

events.title: Lee Foss
events.note: A founder of Hot Creations and one of the people who made the mid-2010s house sound that everything since has been reacting to. From the sweep; the venue reports itself empty.

events.title: Lil Darkie
events.note: Found only in the ticketing sweep; Neck of the Woods is not in this project's source list and no time or price was published. Descriptor is lower-confidence — verify before going.

events.title: Lila Downs (final night)
events.note: Last of three nights in the main hall. No start times published on the only SFJAZZ route that reads.

events.title: Marisa Anderson
events.note: Solo electric guitar that takes American primitive fingerpicking somewhere closer to drone, in a Mission artist-run space with no seats and good acoustics. The Lab is not in this project's source list; from the sweep.

events.title: Muzae Sesay & Alexcia Sundra: Attentive Earth (FOR-SITE at the Guardhouse)
events.note: Two Bay Area painters in FOR-SITE's Guardhouse space, through 24 January. Free, small, and the most consistently well-sited exhibition programme in the city.

events.title: NOTD
events.note: Swedish production duo whose melodic house has a pop writer's instinct for a hook. No door time published on the venue's mirror.

events.title: Smuin Contemporary Ballet: After Hours
events.note: A one-night late programme from the company, separate from French Kiss and listed only on Smuin's own site. No time published anywhere this run could read.

events.title: Tsu Nami
events.note: Melodic bass and future garage on the main floor, the night after the club's Detroit Love anniversary. No door time published.

events.title: Yheti and Toadface with crawdad sniper
events.note: Wonky, deliberately unstable bass music in a 1,000-cap Dogpatch warehouse. The Midway's own calendar renders client-side; this came off Songkick, which is a floor rather than a full picture.

events.title: Free chalk art event
events.note: Chalk handed out along the Ohlone Greenway beside the BART tracks, free, three hours. El Cerrito is in no region list in the brief; filed East Bay by proximity to Albany.

events.title: Science@Cal public lecture
events.note: A working Berkeley researcher giving the public version of their actual work, free, no ticket, Saturday morning. The series has been running for years and is almost never in a listings roundup.

events.title: La maison des bois: episodes 1-3
events.note: Maurice Pialat's 1971 television series about children evacuated to a forest village in the First World War, shown in instalments as it was made. Rarely screened anywhere.

events.title: Wrenching News Workshops
events.note: A making workshop in the museum rather than a lecture. Materials provided; the output is the point.

events.title: Autumn Lights Festival (final night)
events.note: Last of three nights of illuminated sculpture through seven acres of lakeside garden. Saturday is the crowded one; go Thursday if you can and this if you cannot.

events.title: White Nights
events.note: Dostoevsky's story of two insomniacs talking across four nights, filmed. BAMPFA pairs it against the Pialat series in the same afternoon.

events.title: Oakland comedy night at a secret speakeasy
events.note: Two sets, seven and nine, free with a limited code and five dollars off otherwise. Address the day of.

events.title: Elephant Revival
events.note: Colorado string band with a washboard, a fiddle and an actual musical saw, co-presented by folkYEAH!. All ages.

events.title: Fortune Feimster: Takin' Care of Biscuits
events.note: Southern storytelling comedy in a 2,800-cap art deco room. Take BART; the downtown garages shut their gates at seven on weekdays and fill early at weekends.

events.title: ArnoCorps with The Teutonics & The Gum Tree Girls
events.note: A band whose entire body of work is Arnold Schwarzenegger film plots delivered as Austrian-accented heavy rock, and who commit to it with total sincerity. Twenty years in and still the funniest live act in the East Bay. No door time published.

events.title: Damien Escobar
events.note: Electric violin played with an R&B band behind it, which is a more coherent idea than crossover usually manages. Two nights; the ticket link reads as sold out.

events.title: Disney On Ice: Find Your Hero
events.note: Third day of the arena run, with multiple performances. Listed for completeness.

events.title: Last Dinosaurs
events.note: Brisbane guitar-pop, playing Berkeley tonight and again tomorrow, which is unusual for a 300-cap beer hall. No published door time.

events.title: Sam Grisman Project
events.note: David Grisman's son playing the Garcia-Grisman acoustic repertoire outdoors in the hills behind Berkeley. Orinda is in no region list in the brief; filed East Bay by proximity. From the sweep, with no time or price published.

events.title: Dracula: The Musical (matinee)
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: TheatreWorks matinee, downtown Mountain View.

events.title: Hocus Pocus Drag Brunch
events.note: A drag brunch themed to the film, in a comedy club, at one in the afternoon. Exactly the sort of thing the brief means by worthwhile oddity.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera (matinee)
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Sunday matinee, and the penultimate performance of the San Jose stand.

events.title: Day Trip Festival NorCal, day two
events.note: Cloonee headlining, an After Midnight set from Matroda and San Pacho, plus Fallon, Eve Lauren and Sage, with one more guest promised. Sunday is the harder, later-leaning day of the two. 18+.

events.title: Band Capricio
events.note: An early-evening Latin dance band at the Sunnyvale club, half five start. 21+.

events.title: Dracula: The Musical
