events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Sunday evening performance, and the last of the week in Mountain View.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera (closing)
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Final performance of the twelve-day run.

events.title: Dustin Nickerson
events.note: Final show of the weekend run. No per-show time published.

events.title: 54th Annual Half Moon Bay Art & Pumpkin Festival (day two)
events.note: Second and final day. Sunday is marginally calmer than Saturday and Highway 92 is still the problem; the shuttle from the park-and-ride is the answer.

events.title: MUNA with Hemlocke Springs
events.note: The best pop band working in the open-air amphitheatre Stanford spent years restoring, with Hemlocke Springs — whose songs are stranger and funnier than anything else on a bill this size — opening. Stanford is in no region list in the brief; filed Peninsula by proximity. From the sweep, with no curtain time published.

events.title: Nightfall at Filoli
events.note: The lit-garden programme runs nightly through 1 November. No per-night times published on the estate's events index.

events.title: United Nations Association Film Festival
events.note: Sunday of the Palo Alto run. Free for students with ID; the per-film programme could not be read this week.

events.title: Diplo's Run Club: 5K run and rave
events.venue: Robin Williams Meadow, Golden Gate Park
events.note: A 5K starting and finishing in the meadow at half seven in the morning, then a daytime rave with Diplo and guests. Listings disagree on when the set happens — one puts it at nine in the evening — so check before planning the day around it.

events.title: Fort Mason farmers market
events.note: Sunday morning market on the arts campus, free to walk through. Smaller than the Ferry Building's and considerably less of a scrum.

events.title: Filipino American International Book Festival
events.venue: San Francisco Public Library, Main Branch
events.note: Closing day of FilBookFest in the Koret Auditorium. Free.

events.title: S.T.E.A.M. in the Square
events.note: Hands-on science and art for two- to six-year-olds in the square, free. The square's Sunday yoga is explicitly off this week.

events.title: Sundays at the Beach: Tai Chi Day
events.note: Tai chi on the closed Great Highway with the ocean on one side, free, all levels. The promenade's Sunday programming is the best argument anyone has made for keeping the road shut.

events.title: Lindy in the Park
events.note: Free swing dancing on the closed stretch of JFK Drive, every Sunday for thirty years, with a beginner lesson at the start. Weather permitting, which in October it usually is.

events.title: Salvi Soul Sunday block party
events.note: The closing day of the five-day Salvadoran culture gathering, as a free block party folded into Sunday Streets. Pupusas, music and a community that organised this itself.

events.title: San Francisco Photobook Fair
events.note: Forty-plus photobook publishers with tables in the city's municipal photography centre, free. Small-press photography is almost impossible to see in person and this is the one day.

events.title: Shipyard Open Studios, Fall 2026
events.note: Second day of the open studios. Free, free parking, three hundred artists, and the shuttle from the T line runs all afternoon.

events.title: Sunday Streets library open house with music and bubbles
events.note: The branch library throwing its doors open as the street festival passes, with live music outside. Free, and the kind of civic programming that never reaches a ticketing platform.

events.title: Sunday Streets: Excelsior
events.note: Mission Street through the Excelsior closed to cars for five hours, free, with stages, bicycle repair and the neighbourhood's own businesses out on the pavement. The last Sunday Streets of the season and the one in the district that gets the least attention.

events.title: Carter Country
events.note: A documentary on Plains, Georgia, and what a presidency did to a town of six hundred people. Lunchtime slot.

events.title: Imaad Wasif, Black Thumb & Phipps Pt. with Joel St. Julien
events.note: A one o'clock matinee: Imaad Wasif's desert-raga guitar music, plus Joel St. Julien's ambient work. An afternoon bill of this quality in a bar is specific to this venue.

events.title: NAZA
events.note: The Japantown matinee on the run's closing day.

events.title: Assimilation (Word for Word)
events.note: First Sunday matinee of the run, which continues to 8 November on a Wednesday-to-Sunday schedule.

events.title: LOVE SUPREME Day Party with Travie Bobbito, King Most & Bella D.
events.note: Soul, funk and hip-hop on the Chapel's outdoor stage in the afternoon, fifteen dollars, 21+. King Most is one of the best record selectors in the city and this is the cheapest way to hear him.

events.title: Manon (San Francisco Opera)
events.note: The Sunday matinee, second of seven performances. Two o'clock curtain, which makes it the easiest opera to get to from down the Peninsula all season.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Sunday matinee, and the eighth performance of the week. Mischief's disaster-comedy Peter Pan runs to 28 November. The Playhouse's calendar and ticketing pages both returned server errors this run; the production's own page carries the schedule and reads.

events.title: Smuin Contemporary Ballet: French Kiss (closing)
events.note: Final San Francisco performance of Smuin's autumn programme. The Cowell is reachable through no public calendar; only the company's own production page carries these dates.

events.title: Civic Music free concert
events.note: A free concert in the Herbst, RSVP required, donations accepted. Free orchestral and chamber programming in a 900-seat hall is rare enough to put near the top of a Sunday.

events.title: Future of Piano: season opening concert
events.note: New piano music opening a season in the Mission's community music school, with a limited number of free in-person tickets. Thirty dollars otherwise.

events.title: Jigoku (4K restoration)
events.note: Final showing of the restoration on the Japantown screen.

events.title: Roy's World: Barry Gifford's Chicago
events.note: Gifford's autobiographical stories narrated by Willem Dafoe, Matt Dillon and Lili Taylor over archive footage of 1950s Chicago. On the second screen against the Barbara Dane film.

events.title: The 9 Lives of Barbara Dane
events.note: Dane sang blues with Louis Armstrong, founded Paredon Records, and was blacklisted for most of the career she should have had. Part of the Women's Rebel Voices tour that plays the Chapel the same evening — see them in that order.

events.title: Printz Dance Project: Six Degrees of PDP (closing)
events.note: Final performance of the Printz retrospective, four o'clock. ODC's calendar mixes school workshops in with the performances; this is one of the three that are shows.

events.title: Sunday Supper: a Farm to City Feast
events.note: A long communal dinner in the Ferry Building nave with the market's own growers cooking. Ticketed and not cheap; a genuine food event rather than a restaurant promotion.

events.title: Matinee: Gasoline Alley, Big Meat Combo & Class of '77
events.note: A five o'clock punk matinee doubling as a birthday party, listed twice on the venue's ticketing widget under two names at the same hour; it is one show.

events.title: The Scout
events.note: Final weekend screening.

events.title: NAZA
events.note: Last day of the seven-day run, and a second showing in Japantown this afternoon.

events.title: Women's Rebel Voices Film + Music Tour with Miko Marks
events.note: A documentary screening, a Q&A with directors Maureen Gosling and Jed Riffe, and then Miko Marks singing — country music by a Black woman from Flint who was told for twenty years there was no audience. The Barbara Dane film at the Roxie the same afternoon is the companion piece.

events.title: Cobb's Free Comedy Nights: Drag-Up Comedy
events.note: Free with RSVP in a club that normally charges thirty dollars, 18+, two-drink minimum. Drag and stand-up on the same bill.

events.title: Dinosaur Jr. with Stef Chura
events.note: Mascis, Barlow and Murph still touring the original line-up, at a volume the Castro's plaster has not had to deal with often. Sold out. Doors at six for a seven o'clock start.

events.title: Jahan, Low Grade Infection & Vincent Gargiulo
events.note: The evening bill, six hours after the matinee. Kilowatt runs two separate shows today.

events.title: Peaches with SOLTERA, Sola Guinto & Shifters!!
events.note: Twenty-five years of electroclash as performance art, and the live show is still closer to theatre than to a gig. Expensive for the room, and the three support acts are a real bill rather than filler.

events.title: S.F. Comedy Showcase
events.note: The club's long-running Sunday showcase, which has been the city's main proving ground since the 1970s. Standing programming, listed low.

events.title: Sunday Comedy Night
events.note: Free with RSVP downtown, the last of the week's five free Function shows in this digest.

events.title: Big Gay Halloween
events.note: Variety and drag in Chinatown's 1925 opera house, which is one of the best rooms in the city and almost never listed. Twenty dollars.

events.title: Jenna Raine with Zoe Levert
events.note: Teen-pop songwriting with a country inflection. The top of that price range is a meet-and-greet tier, not a seat.

events.title: Pertinence with Oble Reed
events.note: Basement show, eight o'clock. Oble Reed is the Bay Area rapper worth the early door.

events.title: Raaginder with Minz
events.note: A Punjabi-American violinist who plays Hindustani raga lines over hip-hop production, which is a fusion that usually fails and here does not. One of the week's genuinely unusual bookings.

events.title: Sunset Rollercoaster with CLOUDRIVER
events.note: Taipei's most successful band abroad, playing soft-rock city pop with a saxophone and no irony at all. A 2,300-cap room on a Sunday says how deep the diaspora audience runs.

events.title: The Wallflowers with Ragged Glory
events.note: The second of two Bay Area nights after Friday at the Mountain Winery. The Fillmore is the better-sounding room and the worse view.

events.title: heavens to betsy with For Horses & Cut-Rate Druggist
events.note: Second of two nights, with a different support bill — Cut-Rate Druggist carry the riot grrrl lineage forward and For Horses are the odd one out in the good way. If Saturday is gone, this is the same band and the same room.

events.title: Reggae Sunday: Riddim Up
events.note: Roots and dancehall records to finish the week, nine o'clock. Standing Sunday night.

events.title: Alfred Hitchcock's North by Northwest (closing)
events.note: Last day of A.C.T.'s stage version of the Hitchcock film, which has been running since 22 September. No curtain times are published on any A.C.T. page, so this is listed on its stated closing date rather than guessed across the week.

events.title: Cybersentics Book Club: Here/There
events.note: A reading group on technology and embodiment, meeting in public. Monthly; no time published.

events.title: Litquake presents: Menopause Extravaganza
events.note: Writers on menopause, staged in an experimental arts venue rather than a bookshop, which is the most Litquake decision of the festival. No time published on Gray Area's events index.

events.title: Nice As Fuck with Alix Brown (DJ set)
events.note: Jenny Lewis, Erika Forster and Tennessee Thomas reactivating the band they made one record with in 2016 — bass, drums and voice, almost no guitar, and much stranger than Lewis's solo work. A 750-cap room for a reunion nobody expected. No door time published.

events.title: She Wants Revenge
events.note: Mid-2000s dance-punk that was dismissed as Interpol-adjacent and has aged into a genuine goth-club staple. No door time published on the venue's mirror.

events.title: Sunday B3 Sessions
events.note: Hammond organ trio, weekly, free. The most reliable jazz in the city that nobody charges for.

events.title: Thirst Draft: Write Drunk, Edit Never
events.note: A writing night in a bar with the obvious premise, held to properly. No cover published.

events.title: Winslow
events.note: House in the small Folsom Street room. From the sweep; F8 keeps no calendar that a plain fetch reads.

events.title: 5th Annual Berkeley Bird Festival
events.note: Talks, art and guided walks out of the Brower Center into the city's parks, free, with advance registration for the field trips. October is migration and the lists are long.

events.title: Free Oakland Up market
events.note: A free store rather than a market: outdoor items are free to take, one indoor item per person per day, the rest for a donation. Mutual aid with a shopfront.

events.title: Improvisational Screenprinting
events.note: A making workshop in the museum, materials provided.

events.title: Shaihu Umar
events.note: Adamu Halilu's 1976 Nigerian historical film, adapted from a novel by the country's first prime minister. Almost unseeable outside an archive.

events.title: HellaSecret speakeasy comedy and cocktail night
events.note: Free with RSVP, early Sunday, Temescal.

events.title: The King of Comedy
events.note: Scorsese's least-liked film on release and the one that now looks most accurate. Paired with Friday's Raging Bull.

events.title: Epik High: 3.0 North American Tour
events.note: Twenty-three years of Korean hip-hop from a trio who have always been closer to indie rap than to idol pop, and whose live show leans on Tablo's talking as much as the verses.

events.title: Role Model with Samia
events.note: Sold out, in a hillside amphitheatre, in October — bring more clothing than you think. Samia is the better songwriter on the bill and goes on first.

events.title: Damien Escobar
events.note: Second of two nights. The venue publishes the run as a date range rather than per-show times.

events.title: Disney On Ice: Find Your Hero (final day)
events.note: Last day of the arena run. Listed for completeness.

events.title: Eggcorn
events.note: Local band closing the Ivy Room's week. From the sweep; the venue's own site renders client-side and fetches empty.

events.title: Jesse Detor with Mommy Mommy
events.note: Local bill in a small Oakland room, closing the club's week. No published door time.

events.title: Judy Collins
events.note: Eighty-seven years old and still touring the repertoire she defined — the Cohen songs, Both Sides Now, the Sondheim. Presented by Cal Performances; the sweep names the presenter rather than the hall, so the room is unconfirmed. Verify before travelling.

events.title: Last Dinosaurs
events.note: Second Berkeley night in two days. No published door time.

events.title: Rainbow Girls
events.note: Close-harmony folk at a working harbour at the end of a long road, which is half the appeal. Richmond is in no region list in the brief; filed East Bay by proximity. From the sweep, no time published.

events.title: Spotlight Sundays: Roadsongs for Dorothea Lange
events.note: New songs written against Lange's Depression photographs, performed in the museum's James Moore Theater for ten dollars. OMCA holds the Lange archive, which is what makes this more than a themed concert. No time published.
